title: An Extraordinary Act of Political Retribution in Tennessee

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，一档专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 早在黑胶唱片时代的夜总会里当DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每晚你都要带着30万件最珍爱的藏品去上班，你把DJ台变成了一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，里面摆满了精美的50年历史的老物件。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是萨布丽娜·塔韦尼西，这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: In a stunning act of political retribution, Tennessee's Republican-controlled House last week expelled two of its members, both young Black Democrats.
sentences.zh: 在上周，田纳西州由共和党控制的众议院采取了一项令人震惊的政治报复行动，驱逐了两名成员，他们都是年轻的黑人民主党人。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Emily Cochran on the story behind that extraordinary move and what it tells us about this moment in American politics.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事艾米丽·科克伦将为您讲述这一非凡举动背后的故事，以及它向我们透露的当前美国政治现状。

sentences.en: It's Monday, April 10th.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月10日，星期一。

sentences.en: So Emily, you're in Tennessee where we saw this really remarkable vote in the statehouse on Thursday.
sentences.zh: 那么，艾米丽，你现在身处田纳西州，我们在周四亲眼目睹了州议会里那场非常引人注目的投票。

sentences.en: Tell us what happened.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲发生了什么吧。

sentences.en: So the Tennessee House of Representatives voted to expel two lawmakers from the chamber.
sentences.zh: 田纳西州众议院投票决定将两名议员驱逐出议会。

sentences.en: These two men, Justin Jones and Justin Pearson, are two relatively new young Black legislators who represent parts of the state's biggest cities, Nashville and Memphis.
sentences.zh: 这两名男子贾斯汀·琼斯和贾斯汀·皮尔森是两位相对年轻的黑人议员，他们代表着该州最大城市纳什维尔和孟菲斯的部分地区。

sentences.en: This type of thing is incredibly rare since the Civil War era.
sentences.zh: 自内战时期以来，这种事情极其罕见。

sentences.en: It's only happened two times in Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 在田纳西州只发生过两次。

sentences.en: And typically, those expulsions have involved some sort of an investigation, a lawmaker who faced criminal charges or accusations of sexual misconduct.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，这些驱逐行动都涉及某种形式的调查、面临刑事指控或性行为不端指控的议员。

sentences.en: It's not something done lightly.
sentences.zh: 这不是一件轻率做出的决定。

sentences.en: But that wasn't what was going on here.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是这里正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: There was no criminal misconduct.
sentences.zh: 没有任何刑事违纪行为。

sentences.en: So what was going on in this case, Emily?
sentences.zh: 那么艾米丽，这个案子里到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: Like, why exactly were these two lawmakers expelled?
sentences.zh: 比如说，这两名议员究竟为什么被驱逐？

sentences.en: So it came after they led a protest on the House floor.
sentences.zh: 这是在他们领导了一场众议院议事大厅的抗议活动之后发生的。

sentences.en: I think this has a lot to do with an intensifying political divide between blue cities and red states like Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 我认为这与蓝州和红州（例如田纳西州）之间不断加剧的政治分歧有很大关系。

sentences.en: Over time, the state's larger cities, Nashville, Memphis, Knoxville, they have remained defiantly blue,
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，该州较大的城市纳什维尔、孟菲斯、诺克斯维尔，它们依然坚定地保持着民主党阵营的蓝色，

sentences.en: even as the rest of the state has gotten increasingly conservative and taken increasingly hard-line positions.
sentences.zh: 尽管该州其余地区变得越来越保守，并采取了越来越强硬的立场。

sentences.en: And that tension is what we saw essentially blow up this week in Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 这种紧张局势正是我们本周在田纳西州看到彻底爆发的本质。

sentences.en: Right, these little blue dots in the sea of red, right?
sentences.zh: 没错，红色海洋中的这些蓝色小点，对吧？

sentences.en: So let's talk about that.
sentences.zh: 那我们来谈谈这个。

sentences.en: Give me a sense of what those political changes have looked like in Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 让我了解一下田纳西州的这些政治变化是什么样的。

sentences.en: So it's similar to what we have seen in other states nationally, right?
sentences.zh: 这类似于我们在全国其他州看到的情况，对吧？

sentences.en: This used to be a state that was somewhat mixed politically.
sentences.zh: 这里过去曾是一个政治立场有些混杂的州。

sentences.en: But it's become increasingly more conservative, voting for every Republican candidate in a presidential election since the 90s.
sentences.zh: 但它变得越来越保守，自20世纪90年代以来，在历次总统大选中都投给每一位共和党候选人。

sentences.en: You know, in 2020, 60% of the vote went for Donald Trump, Bill Lee, the Republican governor, won handily.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在2020年，60%的选票投给了唐纳德·特朗普，共和党州长比尔·李轻松获胜。

sentences.en: So Republicans have dominated state politics, and it's allowed them in the last few months to pass and propose a bunch of bills on culture war issues.
sentences.zh: 因此，共和党人一直主导着州政坛，这使他们在过去几个月里得以通过和提出一堆关于文化战争议题的法案。

sentences.en: And there's a supermajority in the legislature.
sentences.zh: 而且立法机构中存在超级多数。

sentences.en: So we've seen a lot of legislation targeting the rights of LGBTQ people in this state.
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到了大量针对该州LGBTQ群体权益的立法。

sentences.en: Gun laws have steadily weakened.
sentences.zh: 枪支法律稳步放宽。

sentences.en: And abortion access is nonexistent after the fall of Roe.
sentences.zh: 罗诉韦德案倒台后，堕胎途径不复存在。

sentences.en: And Emily, what about the cities?
sentences.zh: 艾米丽，那这些城市呢？

sentences.en: I mean, talk to me about how those have changed.
sentences.zh: 我是说，跟我聊聊这些城市是怎么改变的。

sentences.en: So the cities in Tennessee are some of the fastest-growing urban areas in the country.
sentences.zh: 田纳西州的城市是全国发展最快的城市地区之一。

sentences.en: You've had an influx of tech workers, immigrants, all kinds of people coming from out of state and moving here to the cities.
sentences.zh: 这里涌入了科技工作者、移民以及从州外来到这里搬到城市的各种各样的人。

sentences.en: And I think with that, you've also seen a stronger progressive base in the city.
sentences.zh: 我认为随之而来的是，你在城市里也看到了更强大的进步派基础。

sentences.en: They are electing more liberal Democrats.
sentences.zh: 他们正在选举更多自由派的民主党人。

sentences.en: And as Republicans push through more conservative policies,
sentences.zh: 随着共和党人强行推行更多保守政策，

sentences.en: it's getting harder and harder for Democrats to see how to be friends with people who are trying to take away access to health care for their children and clamping down on social issues that are really important to them.
sentences.zh: 民主党人越来越难以弄清楚，如何去和那些试图剥夺他们孩子的医疗保健服务、并打压对他们至关重要的社会议题的人做朋友。

sentences.en: And then...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: Another deadly school shooting in America, this time at a Christian school in Nashville.
sentences.zh: 美国又发生了一起致命的校园枪击案，这次是在纳什维尔的一所基督教学校。

sentences.en: Two weeks ago, there's a mass shooting.
sentences.zh: 两周前，发生了一起大规模枪击事件。

sentences.en: The suspect, identified as a 28-year-old former student, shot and killed three young children and three adults before being killed by police.
sentences.zh: 嫌疑人被确定为一名28岁的前学生，他开枪打死了三名幼童和三名成年人，随后被警方击毙。

sentences.en: It shocks a very close-knit church community.
sentences.zh: 这震惊了一个非常紧密的教会社区。

sentences.en: And a lot of people in Nashville are grieving.
sentences.zh: 纳什维尔的许多人都感到悲痛。

sentences.en: These parents, their lives are changed forever today.
sentences.zh: 这些父母的生活在今天永远改变了。

sentences.en: Forever.
sentences.zh: 永远。

sentences.en: I mean, we got three nine-year-old babies that aren't going to make it home to them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们有三个九岁的宝贝再也回不了家了。

sentences.en: And then it brings us to a familiar place politically.
sentences.zh: 然后这把我们带回了一个熟悉的政治境地。

sentences.en: Ladies and gentlemen, this could happen anywhere.
sentences.zh: 女士们先生们，这种事可能发生在任何地方。

sentences.en: It happened here today.
sentences.zh: 它今天就发生在这里。

sentences.en: But unless we take action, it's going to happen again.
sentences.zh: 但除非我们采取行动，否则它还会再次发生。

sentences.en: Where there's an immediate push for gun restrictions.
sentences.zh: 这里立即出现了对枪支限制的呼声。

sentences.en: I didn't have one person ask me for thoughts and prayers today.
sentences.zh: 今天没有一个人向我索要思念和祈祷。

sentences.en: They asked me for courage to come down here and do something.
sentences.zh: 他们向我索要勇气，来到这里做点什么。

sentences.en: And Republicans make it clear that their focus is not going to be on guns.
sentences.zh: 而共和党人明确表示，他们的重点不会放在枪支上。

sentences.en: I believe that we ought to have an armed guard in every school in Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 我相信我们应该在田纳西州的每一所学校里配备武装警卫。

sentences.en: But it's going to be on toughening school security.
sentences.zh: 而是会放在加强学校安全上。

sentences.en: $140 million for public schools to hire SROs and highly trained guards.
sentences.zh: 为公立学校拨款1.4亿美元用于聘请学校资源警官和训练有素的警卫。

sentences.en: There is no excuse to not have a guard at every school.
sentences.zh: 没有任何借口不在每一所学校配备警卫。

sentences.en: Pouring millions of dollars into school resource officers and stricter security protocols at public and private schools.
sentences.zh: 投入数百万美元用于公立和私立学校的学校资源警官和更严格的安全协议。

sentences.en: And in the days after the shooting, hundreds of people march to the state legislature, rally at the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 枪击事件发生后的几天里，数百人游行前往州立法机构，在国会大厦集会。

sentences.en: I really just want to fight for gun control because I'm tired of my life being put second to a firearm.
sentences.zh: 我真的只是想为枪支管控而战，因为我厌倦了我的生命被置于枪械之后。

sentences.en: Students, parents and teachers demand that the legislature take action to toughen gun laws.
sentences.zh: 学生、家长和老师要求立法机构采取行动收紧枪支法律。

sentences.en: We just don't have a government here in Tennessee that's willing to do anything about gun laws.
sentences.zh: 我们在田纳西州就是没有一个愿意对枪支法律做点什么的政府。

sentences.en: And in the middle of all these protests, that's when we first hear about three Democratic representatives.
sentences.zh: 就在所有这些抗议活动进行的正中间，我们第一次听说了三位民主党议员。

sentences.en: Justin Jones, Justin Pearson, and a woman from Knoxville named Gloria Johnson.
sentences.zh: 贾斯汀·琼斯、贾斯汀·皮尔森，以及一位来自诺克斯维尔名叫格洛丽亚·约翰逊的女性。

sentences.en: So tell me more about these three lawmakers.
sentences.zh: 那么，多跟我讲讲这三位议员吧。

sentences.en: Who are they?
sentences.zh: 他们是谁？

sentences.en: So Justin Jones and Justin Pearson are some of the youngest members of the House.
sentences.zh: 贾斯汀·琼斯和贾斯汀·皮尔森是众议院最年轻的几位成员。

sentences.en: They're both in their late 20s.
sentences.zh: 他们俩都二十多岁快三十岁。

sentences.en: They're both Black community organizers who have recently been elevated from being familiar faces in sit-ins and protests to the legislature, to a position of power.
sentences.zh: 他们都是黑人社区组织者，最近从静坐抗议活动中的熟悉面孔晋升到了立法机构，进入了权力位置。

sentences.en: Jones won his election in the November midterms to represent parts of Nashville.
sentences.zh: 琼斯在11月的中期选举中赢得选举，代表纳什维尔的部分地区。

sentences.en: This came after he led a 61-day protest for racial justice outside the state capitol in the aftermath of the death of George Floyd in 2020.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，他在2020年乔治·弗洛伊德之死后，在州国会大厦外领导了一场持续61天的争取种族公正的抗议活动。

sentences.en: So he is a familiar face to lawmakers and a thorn in the side of this Republican majority.
sentences.zh: 因此，他是立法者们熟悉的面孔，也是这个共和党多数派的心头大患。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: So what about Pearson?
sentences.zh: 那么皮尔森呢？

sentences.en: So he won a special election in January to represent parts of Memphis.
sentences.zh: 他在1月份的一场特别选举中获胜，代表孟菲斯的部分地区。

sentences.en: He helped lead a successful campaign against the construction of a crude oil pipeline that would have cut through a mostly Black neighborhood in Memphis.
sentences.zh: 他曾协助领导了一场反对建设一条原油管道的成功运动，该管道原本会穿过孟菲斯一个主要为黑人的社区。

sentences.en: And even in the few weeks that he's been in the legislature, he's also emerged as one of the most outspoken members,
sentences.zh: 甚至在他进入立法机构的短短几周内，他也崭露头角，成为了最直言不讳的成员之一，

sentences.en: especially after tragedies like the killing of Tyree Nichols in Memphis.
sentences.zh: 特别是在经历了孟菲斯泰瑞·尼科尔斯被杀等悲剧之后。

sentences.en: So in other words, a younger generation of Democrat, as you say,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，正如你所说，这是年轻一代的民主党人，

sentences.en: much more progressive and coming directly out of the activism and energy that followed the killing of George Floyd in 2020.
sentences.zh: 更加进步，并且直接脱胎于2020年乔治·弗洛伊德遇害后随之而来的激进主义和活力。

sentences.en: What about the third lawmaker?
sentences.zh: 第三位议员呢？

sentences.en: So Gloria Johnson is a white lawmaker from Knoxville.
sentences.zh: 格洛丽亚·约翰逊是来自诺克斯维尔的白人女议员。

sentences.en: She's a retired teacher and she's been serving on the legislature on and off for the last 10 years.
sentences.zh: 她是一名退休教师，在过去10年里断断续续地在立法机构任职。

sentences.en: She has talked a lot about how gun violence affected her personally as a teacher when there was a fatal shooting on her school campus.
sentences.zh: 她曾多次谈到枪支暴力作为一名教师如何对她产生个人影响，当时她的学校校园曾发生过致命枪击事件。

sentences.en: And in fact, all three of them have been very open about how their lives and their activism brought them to politics.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们三人都非常坦诚地讲述了他们的生活和激进主义是如何将他们带入政治的。

sentences.en: So what did the three lawmakers do as protests erupt in the Tennessee legislature?
sentences.zh: 那么，当抗议活动在田纳西州立法机构爆发时，这三位议员做了什么？

sentences.en: So last Thursday, days after the shooting, protesters have again packed the building, packed the galleries of the chamber.
sentences.zh: 上周四，枪击事件发生几天后，抗议者再次挤满了大楼，挤满了议事大厅的旁听席。

sentences.en: And Republicans are proceeding with legislation as usual.
sentences.zh: 而共和党人则照常推进立法。

sentences.en: This bill is designed to help a small community in my district that missed a deadline to have their wine and grocery store referendum.
sentences.zh: 这项法案旨在帮助我选区的一个小社区，他们错过了一个截止日期，未能举行其葡萄酒和杂货店全民公决。

sentences.en: And every time one of these Democrats tries to pivot the debate.
sentences.zh: 而每当这些民主党人试图转移辩论焦点时。

sentences.en: I want to start with we need to do something about gun control.
sentences.zh: 我想从我们必须对枪支管控做点什么开始说起。

sentences.en: To turn the debate to gun control, to an acknowledgement of the hundreds of people in the building.
sentences.zh: 将辩论转向枪支管控，转向对大楼里数百人的承认。

sentences.en: Representative Pearson, stay on the bill.
sentences.zh: 皮尔森议员，请回到法案本身。

sentences.en: I don't want to have to start ruling out order again.
sentences.zh: 我不想再次开始裁定违规。

sentences.en: Their microphones are turned off and they're told to stay on topic.
sentences.zh: 他们的麦克风被关掉了，并被告知要扣紧主题。

sentences.en: Representative Pearson.
sentences.zh: 皮尔森议员。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Again, we need to do something about gun control.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我们需要对枪支管控做点什么。

sentences.en: Representative Pearson, this is your last warning.
sentences.zh: 皮尔森议员，这是你的最后一次警告。

sentences.en: Either stay on the bill or you will not be called on.
sentences.zh: 要么回到法案本身，要么你将不会被点名发言。

sentences.en: This is your last warning.
sentences.zh: 这是你的最后一次警告。

sentences.en: I'm asking you politely to stay on the bill.
sentences.zh: 我客气地请你回到法案本身。

sentences.en: So eventually they get up, they walk to the front of the room, which is what people call the well of the chamber.
sentences.zh: 所以他们最终站起身来，走到房间的最前方，也就是人们所说的议事大厅的井字区。

sentences.en: They have a megaphone.
sentences.zh: 他们拿着一个扩音器。

sentences.en: They have a sign that says, protect kids, not guns.
sentences.zh: 他们举着一块牌子，上面写着：保护孩子，而不是保护枪支。

sentences.en: And they begin to lead the protesters in chants.
sentences.zh: 他们开始带领抗议者高喊口号。

sentences.en: Leaves that allow us to be silent in the face of injustice.
sentences.zh: 让我们在面对不公时保持沉默的叶子。

sentences.en: Power to the people.
sentences.zh: 权力归于人民。

sentences.en: And the entire proceeding grinds to a halt.
sentences.zh: 整个议程戛然而止。

sentences.en: They literally are stopping the proceeding with a bullhorn.
sentences.zh: 他们竟然用大音箱叫喊来阻止议程。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And there are cheering on these protesters, encouraging them.
sentences.zh: 抗议者们在一旁为他们欢呼，鼓励他们。

sentences.en: We can never put each and every one of you our proof that we will not be silent.
sentences.zh: 我们永远可以把你们每一个人作为我们不会保持沉默的证据。

sentences.en: And so thank you for being here.
sentences.zh: 所以感谢你们来到这里。

sentences.en: Thank all your colleagues for being here.
sentences.zh: 感谢你们所有的同事来到这里。

sentences.en: You are being heard and listened to and we will not quit.
sentences.zh: 你们正在被听见、被倾听，我们绝不会放弃。

sentences.en: And the House goes into recess because Republicans don't know what to do.
sentences.zh: 众议院随即宣布休会，因为共和党人不知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: And they're scrambling to regain control of the day.
sentences.zh: 他们正手忙脚乱地重新掌控当天的局面。

sentences.en: By the time the whole thing ends, it's about 40 to 50 minutes.
sentences.zh: 当整件事结束时，大约过去了40到50分钟。

sentences.en: But it's clear Republicans are furious about what has just happened.
sentences.zh: 但很明显，共和党人对刚刚发生的事情感到愤怒。

sentences.en: The Speaker of the House, Cameron Sexton, goes so far as to compare what happened to the violent riot on January 6, 2021.

sentences.en: These are two state legislators who have now been elevated to a national profile.
sentences.zh: 这两位州议员如今已经跃升为全国瞩目的焦点人物。

sentences.en: Given the opportunity, with the eyes of the nation on them, all kinds of national media watching, to preach about gun violence, the need to restrict gun access,
sentences.zh: 在全国目光的注视下、在各类国家级媒体的围观下，他们顺理成章地宣讲枪支暴力、限制枪支获取的必要性、

sentences.en: racism in their state, and their support for these young protesters.
sentences.zh: 他们州存在的种族主义问题，以及他们对这些年轻抗议者的支持。

sentences.en: And now you've seen everyone from former President Barack Obama, President Biden, all of these national Democrats weigh in, talk about how unfair and undemocratic this was,
sentences.zh: 现在你可以看到，从前总统巴拉克·奥巴马到拜登总统，所有这些全国性的民主党人都纷纷发声，谴责此举如何不公正、如何反民主，

sentences.en: circulate fundraising links.
sentences.zh: 并广为转发筹款链接。

sentences.en: They've raised thousands of dollars in the days since.
sentences.zh: 在随后的几天里，他们已经筹集了数千美元。

sentences.en: I mean, respectfully, I don't think a lot of people outside of the state of Tennessee would have necessarily known about them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，恕我直言，田纳西州以外的很多人原本未必知道他们是谁。

sentences.en: And here we are.
sentences.zh: 而现在他们名声大噪了。

sentences.en: But what, at a practical level, will happen to them?
sentences.zh: 但从实际层面上讲，他们将面临怎样的命运？

sentences.en: So there's a very real possibility this ends with them back in the state legislature.
sentences.zh: 因此，有一种非常现实的可能性，那就是这最终会让他们重返州议会。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: How?
sentences.zh: 怎么做？

sentences.en: So under the rules governing this whole process, the governing bodies in their counties can appoint someone to fill the seat until a special election.
sentences.zh: 根据管辖整个程序的规则，他们所在县的管理机构可以任命某人填补空缺席位，直至举行特别选举。

sentences.en: And in Nashville, it seems pretty clear that there are the votes to name Jones back to that open seat as early as Monday.
sentences.zh: 在纳什维尔，情况似乎很明朗，最快在周一就会有足够的票数重新任命琼斯填补那个空缺席位。

sentences.en: Oh my gosh.
sentences.zh: 我的天哪。

sentences.en: And it's likely that both men will run again for their seats.
sentences.zh: 而且这两位男性很可能会再次竞选他们的席位。

sentences.en: And they will do so now with a war chest filled with donations from appreciative voters across the country.
sentences.zh: 这一次，他们将带着装满全国各地感激选民捐款的竞选资金卷土重来。

sentences.en: So, Emily, I'm listening to your telling of this story and thinking, really, you know, this did not go that badly for these lawmakers.
sentences.zh: 所以，埃米莉，听你讲完这个故事，我在想，真的，你知道的，这对这些议员来说其实结果并不算太糟。

sentences.en: On the contrary, it raised their national profile.
sentences.zh: 恰恰相反，这提升了他们在全国的知名度。

sentences.en: They now have a war cheSt.
sentences.zh: 他们现在有了充足的竞选资金。

sentences.en: And, you know, in some ways, I don't know, to me it looks like own goal for Republicans, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，在某些方面，我不知道，在我看来这就像是共和党人自摆乌龙，对吧？

sentences.en: This kind of backfired.
sentences.zh: 这有点适得其反了。

sentences.en: I think that's why a lot of people in this state, a lot of political observers,
sentences.zh: 我想这也是为什么州内的许多民众和政治观察人士，

sentences.en: are almost bewildered about why the Republicans chose to pick this fight and chose to give them this kind of platform.
sentences.zh: 都对共和党人为何选择挑起这场争端、为何给他们提供这样一个平台感到困惑不解。

sentences.en: I will say, the conservative base is pretty happy with what happened.
sentences.zh: 不过我得说，保守派基层对发生的事情相当满意。

sentences.en: And in a state where, quite frankly, the majority of elections are now decided in Republican primaries as opposed to general elections, for lawmakers, I think that's what matters.
sentences.zh: 在一个坦率地说绝大多数选举如今由共和党初选而非大选决定的州里，对议员们来说，这才是最重要的。

sentences.en: The hard right is praising them for fighting, for showing how to deal with a so-called insurrection.
sentences.zh: 极右翼正称赞他们敢于抗争，展示了如何应对所谓的“叛乱”。

sentences.en: This is what happens now.
sentences.zh: 这就是现在的现状。

sentences.en: They're happy with this.
sentences.zh: 他们对这个结果很满意。

sentences.en: They say this is how it should be done.
sentences.zh: 他们说事情本来就该这么做。

sentences.en: So, Emily, in some ways, this is where we are with politics in America right now, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，埃米莉，在某些方面，这就是我们现在美国政治的现状，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, each side speaking only to its base, not to each other.
sentences.zh: 比如，双方都只对自己的核心选民说话，而没有互相交流。

sentences.en: It's really like a performance intended for an audience that's sometimes even outside the state completely.
sentences.zh: 这真的很像是一场表演，是专门为了一个有时甚至完全不在本州的观众准备的。

sentences.en: Like, the more traditional route for these lawmakers who felt unheard in some ways would have been to work within the system,
sentences.zh: 比如，对于那些在某些方面感到诉求被忽视的议员来说，更传统的做法本该是在体制内工作，

sentences.en: focus on changing the power dynamic from the inside by persuading voters in elections, right?
sentences.zh: 通过在选举中说服选民，专注于从内部改变权力动态，对吧？

sentences.en: But that's not what happened.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: Right, because if you're one of these Democrats, how do you find compromise with this particular brand of Republican majority?
sentences.zh: 没错，因为如果你是这些民主党人中的一员，你又怎么能和这种特定风格的共和党多数派达成妥协呢？

sentences.en: This is a Republican supermajority that is willing to wield their power in what seems like any way they can to squash concern or pushback from these Democrats who represent these little blue dots in red states.
sentences.zh: 这是一个共和党超级多数派，他们愿意以似乎能用尽的一切方式来行使权力，以压制那些在红州中代表着蓝色小点的民主党人的担忧或反弹。

sentences.en: So, even if ultimately these Democratic lawmakers end up back in their seats, the fact that Republicans took this step at all, I think, raises concerns about the precedent it sets,
sentences.zh: 所以，即便这些民主党议员最终还是回到了他们的席位上，但共和党人采取这一步的做法，我认为，还是引发了人们对它所开创的先例的担忧，

sentences.en: not only in Tennessee, but across the country, about the steps a supermajority is willing to take to punish duly elected members of the minority.
sentences.zh: 不仅在田纳西州，而且在全美范围内，人们都在担忧一个超级多数派为了惩罚少数派中合法当选的成员，愿意采取到什么地步的手段。

sentences.en: Emily, thank you.
sentences.zh: 埃米莉，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我编写了“连线”这款游戏，这是《纽约时报》字谜游戏之一，我也很喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，我也喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天都制作“拼写蜜蜂”和“字母箱”这两款游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我还有一种叫做联觉的现象。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚刚听到声音的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games，今天就开始游玩。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该了解的其他消息。

sentences.en: On Friday night, a federal judge in Texas issued a preliminary ruling invalidating the federal government's 23-year-old approval of the abortion pill, Mifepristone.
sentences.zh: 周五晚上，德克萨斯州的一名联邦法官发布了一项初步裁决，宣布联邦政府对堕胎药米非司酮长达23年的批准无效。

sentences.en: It was an unprecedented order that, if it survives court challenges, could make it harder to get abortions in states like New York and California, where the procedure is legal.
sentences.zh: 这是一项前所未有的命令，如果它在法庭诉讼中存活下来，可能会使在纽约和加利福尼亚等堕胎合法的州获得堕胎服务变得更加困难。

sentences.en: The drug, part of a two-pill regimen that accounts for about half of all abortions in the country, will continue to be available in the short term.
sentences.zh: 这种药物属于双药方案的一部分，该方案占全国所有堕胎手术的大约一半，在短期内它将继续可用。

sentences.en: The judge, Matthew Kasmarek, suspended his own ruling for a week to give the federal government time to ask an appeals court to intervene.
sentences.zh: 法官马修·卡斯马雷克将他自己的裁决暂停了一周，以为联邦政府争取时间要求上诉法院介入。

sentences.en: Less than an hour after the ruling came down, a judge in Washington state issued another ruling, which contradicted that of the Texas judge.
sentences.zh: 在该裁决下达不到一小时后，华盛顿州的一名法官发布了另一项裁决，与德克萨斯州法官的裁决相矛盾。

sentences.en: The conflicting orders appear to create a legal standoff that will likely end up in the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 这些相互冲突的命令似乎造成了一种法律对峙，最终很可能会闹到最高法院。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Asta Cetarvedi, Ricky Navecki, Will Reed, Alex Stern, and Diana Nguyen.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由阿斯塔·切塔韦迪、里奇·纳韦基、威尔·里德、亚历克斯·斯特恩和戴安娜·阮制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Mark George, Lisa Chow, and Patricia Willans.
sentences.zh: 节目由马克·乔治、莉萨·周和帕特里夏·威兰斯剪辑。

sentences.en: Contains original music by Marian Lozano and Rowan Nemisto.
sentences.zh: 包含玛丽安·洛扎诺和罗万·内米斯托的原创音乐。

sentences.en: And was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由克里斯·伍德进行工程制作。

sentences.en: Special thanks to William Davis.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢威廉·戴维斯。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Lansford of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由来自 Wonderly 的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯福德创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔韦尼西。

sentences.en: We'll see you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我们明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《电线cutter秀》上，我们将为假期接待客人做好准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让你的客人感到宾至如归的技巧。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是深度睡眠者吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是喝断片去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是指，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症吗，对食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何地方查找《电线cutter秀》。
